excerpt: We commit to the following governance measures to promote internal and external accountability.
paraphrase: Anthropic states it commits to governance measures for internal and external accountability.

excerpt: Responsible Scaling Officer: We will maintain the position of RSO, a designated member of staff who is responsible for the implementation of this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain an RSO position responsible for implementing the policy.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (1) as needed, proposing updates to this policy; (2) approving relevant model development or deployment decisions based on our risk assessments; (3) reviewing major contracts (e.g., deployment partnerships) for consistency with this policy;
paraphrase: The RSO's duties include proposing policy updates, approving development/deployment decisions, and reviewing major contracts for policy consistency.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (4) overseeing the implementation of this policy, including the allocation of sufficient resources; (5) receiving and addressing reports of potential instances of noncompliance; and (6) making judgment calls on policy interpretation and application.
paraphrase: The RSO's duties also include overseeing implementation and resourcing, handling noncompliance reports, and making interpretive judgment calls.

excerpt: Long Term Benefit Trust: We will regularly brief the LTBT on plans and developments related to our Risk Reports, including model training, capability evals, mitigations, and risk analyses.
paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly brief the LTBT on Risk Report-related plans and developments.

excerpt: Internal transparency: We will share final, unredacted Risk Reports with a large number of Anthropic employees (at least 200).
paraphrase: Anthropic will share final, unredacted Risk Reports with at least 200 employees.

excerpt: We will share minimally-redacted Risk Reports with all of Anthropic's regular-clearance staff.
paraphrase: Anthropic will share minimally-redacted Risk Reports with all regular-clearance staff.

excerpt: Noncompliance reporting: We will maintain a process for Anthropic staff to submit anonymous or identified reports regarding potential noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a process for staff to submit anonymous or identified noncompliance reports.

excerpt: Staff will have more than one option for who receives these reports, including the RSO, and at least one executive who does not report to the RSO.
paraphrase: Staff will have multiple reporting options, including the RSO and at least one non-reporting executive.

excerpt: When we receive a report, we will promptly investigate, take appropriate and proportional corrective action if it is substantiated, and document the report and our findings.
paraphrase: Upon receiving a report, Anthropic will investigate promptly, take proportional action if substantiated, and document findings.

excerpt: We will provide quarterly updates to the Board regarding reports of potential noncompliance, whether substantiated or not.
paraphrase: Anthropic will give the Board quarterly updates on noncompliance reports regardless of substantiation.

excerpt: If we determine that a report is (1) substantiated and (2) involves a material safety risk, we will promptly notify the Board and we may provide public notice of the same.
paraphrase: If a report is substantiated and involves material safety risk, the Board will be notified promptly and public notice may follow.

excerpt: Finally, we will protect reporters from retaliation, and where a report concerns the conduct of the RSO, at least one recipient will be a member of the Board.
paraphrase: Reporters will be protected from retaliation, and reports concerning the RSO must reach at least one Board member.

excerpt: Employee agreements: We will not impose contractual non-disparagement obligations on employees, candidates, or former employees in a way that could impede or discourage them from publicly raising safety concerns about Anthropic.
paraphrase: Anthropic will not impose non-disparagement obligations that discourage public safety concerns.

excerpt: If we offer agreements with a non-disparagement clause, that clause will not preclude raising safety concerns, nor will it preclude disclosure of the existence of that clause.
paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clause offered will not preclude raising safety concerns or disclosing its existence.

excerpt: Internal review: We will regularly conduct an internal review of our implementation of this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly conduct internal reviews of policy implementation.

excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an approximately annual third-party review of adherence to procedural commitments.

excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes.
paraphrase: The compliance review focuses on procedure rather than substantive outcomes.

excerpt: Policy changes: Changes to the RSP will be proposed by the CEO and RSO, and approved by the Board in consultation with the LTBT.
paraphrase: RSP changes are proposed by the CEO and RSO and approved by the Board in consultation with the LTBT.

excerpt: If we update the RSP, we will publicly share the updated version prior to or on its effective date and will record the differences from the prior draft in the Change Log.
paraphrase: Updated RSP versions will be publicly shared by their effective date with differences recorded in the Change Log.

excerpt: We will maintain the current version of the RSP on our website.
paraphrase: The current RSP version will be kept on Anthropic's website.

section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors

paraphrase: The listed commitments do not prevent Anthropic from taking cautionary action in other circumstances.

locator: Table Appendix A / General upleveling / Commitment
excerpt: We will make a significant effort to meet or exceed that performance standard. However, we will not necessarily delay AI development and deployment in this scenario.
paraphrase: Anthropic will make a significant effort to match or exceed the standard, but will not necessarily delay development or deployment.

excerpt: Earlier editions of our RSP defined "AI Safety Levels" with specific lists of required controls. We still use this concept to refer to, and distinguish between, present levels of risk mitigations—those that we maintain for existing AI models.
paraphrase: Earlier RSP editions defined ASLs with specific control lists; the concept is still used to describe current risk mitigation levels for existing models.

excerpt: This and other italicized instances of "highly capable" use the term as defined in Section 3.6.
paraphrase: Footnote clarifying that italicized uses of "highly capable" refer to the Section 3.6 definition.

excerpt: (For example, our initial Risk Report uses this distinction.) However, when defining the risk mitigations needed for future levels of AI capability, we have found that providing a specific list of controls is overly rigid,
paraphrase: The initial Risk Report uses this distinction, but Anthropic found specific control lists too rigid for defining future capability levels.

excerpt: and we instead prefer to focus on what sort of argument an AI developer should make (and what sorts of actors it should address) regarding the risk level from its systems.
paraphrase: Anthropic prefers focusing on the kind of argument and actors addressed regarding system risk level rather than rigid control lists.

excerpt: September 19, 2023 (RSP v1.0) RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
paraphrase: The initial RSP version was released September 19, 2023.

excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The 2024 update introduced a more flexible risk-management approach while retaining the no-deployment-without-safeguards commitment.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key 2024 improvements included new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes, and new governance/external-input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The most notable changes are described below.

excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models).
paraphrase: The ASL term now refers to safeguard groups rather than also referring to models.

excerpt: We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards. This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: New concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards were introduced to allow more targeted safeguard application.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The prior ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint for autonomous AI capabilities.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint prompts additional evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation instead of automatic escalation.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
paraphrase: Previously these capabilities triggered increased safeguards as a provisional threshold pending better threat understanding.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic now believes those capability levels would not require the ASL-3 standard.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / AI R&D threshold added
excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / AI R&D threshold added
excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
paraphrase: These capabilities could cause rapid unpredictable AI advances outpacing risk evaluation, and may warn of R&D automation in other domains.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Instead of prespecified evaluations, an affirmative case is now required showing models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
paraphrase: Predefined tests risk missing emerging threats or being overly conservative.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board pre-approve evaluations.
paraphrase: Because tests change frequently, this approach is more practical than Board pre-approval of evaluations.

excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4× Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence was changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from three months.
stated_bar: 4× Effective Compute or six months (previously three months)

excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
paraphrase: The three-month cadence had forced prioritization of frequent evaluations over comprehensive testing and methodology improvement.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6× buffer), with more general requirements
paraphrase: Specific prior methodology elements, like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer, were replaced with more general requirements.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
paraphrase: The general requirements aim to match adversary effort levels and provide informal estimates of future scaling impacts.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Evaluation science is not yet mature enough to confidently set a precise buffer to a Capability Threshold, though this remains an aspiration.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were updated to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them.
paraphrase: Instead of specific safeguard details, overall security/deployment standards and their requirements are now specified.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
paraphrase: This change allows more flexible safeguard adaptation as understanding improves.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models: We have clarified which actors are in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The actors in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard were clarified.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: We also removed the commitment to protect against scaled attacks and distillation attacks from the ASL-2 Security standard.
paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security standard's commitment to protect against scaled and distillation attacks was removed.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Distillation remains a concern for more capable models, but ASL-2 models have not reached harmful Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard was updated to allow safeguard levels to vary by deployment context.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming.
paraphrase: General access systems still require passing intensive red-teaming.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: For internal use, safety testing and deployments to sufficiently trusted users, we will instead require a combination of access controls and monitoring.
paraphrase: For internal use and sufficiently trusted-user deployments, a combination of access controls and monitoring will be required instead.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: New Capability and Safeguards Reports: We have introduced Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports.
paraphrase: Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports were newly introduced.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: We expect that aggregating all the available evidence about model capabilities will provide decision makers with a more complete picture of the overall level of risk and improve our ability to solicit feedback on our work.
paraphrase: Aggregating capability evidence is expected to give decision-makers a fuller risk picture and improve feedback solicitation.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Internal and external accountability
excerpt: Internal and external accountability: We have made a number of changes to our previous "procedural commitments."
paraphrase: A number of changes were made to the previous procedural commitments.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Internal and external accountability
excerpt: These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer; adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments;
paraphrase: Changes included expanding RSO duties and adding internal critique and external expert input on assessments.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Internal and external accountability
excerpt: new procedures related to internal governance; and maintaining a public page for overviews of past Capability and Safeguard Reports, RSP-related updates, and future plans.
paraphrase: Changes also included new internal governance procedures and a public page summarizing past reports, updates, and future plans.

excerpt: RSP-2025: This update clarifies which Capability Thresholds would require enhanced safeguards beyond our current ASL-3 standards. The key changes include:
paraphrase: The 2025 update clarifies which Capability Thresholds require safeguards beyond ASL-3.

excerpt: New Capability Thresholds: We have added a new capability threshold related to CBRN development, which defines capabilities that could substantially uplift the development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs.
paraphrase: A new CBRN-related capability threshold was added, defining capabilities that could substantially uplift moderately resourced state programs.

excerpt: We have also disaggregated our existing AI R&D capability thresholds, separating them into two distinct levels (the ability to fully automate entry-level AI research work, and the ability to cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling) and provided additional detail on the corresponding Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: The AI R&D capability thresholds were split into two levels—full automation of entry-level research and dramatic acceleration of effective scaling—with more safeguard detail added.

excerpt: Iterative Commitment: We have adopted a general commitment to reevaluate our Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade to a new set of Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: A general commitment was adopted to reevaluate Capability Thresholds whenever safeguards are upgraded.

excerpt: We have decided not to maintain a commitment to define ASL-N+1 evaluations by the time we develop ASL-N models; such an approach would add unnecessary complexity because Capability Thresholds do not naturally come grouped in discrete levels.
paraphrase: Anthropic dropped the commitment to predefine next-level evaluations by the time current-level models are developed, since thresholds don't naturally group discretely.

excerpt: We believe it is more practical and sensible instead to commit to reconsidering the whole list of Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade our safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic finds it more practical to reconsider the entire list of Capability Thresholds upon each safeguard upgrade.

excerpt: ASL-3 Security: This update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Security Standard now excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders.

excerpt: Previously, only "highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders" were explicitly excluded.
paraphrase: Previously only highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders were explicitly excluded.

excerpt: The model capabilities and threat models corresponding with the ASL-3 Security Standard do not warrant protection against either group:
paraphrase: The capabilities and threat models associated with ASL-3 Security do not justify protecting against either insider group.

excerpt: the CBRN-3 threat models entail large numbers of users having access to unguarded models (which is more likely to occur through a universal jailbreak than via model theft), and the relatively small number of employees who might be capable of model theft does not significantly affect the risk level.
paraphrase: CBRN-3 threat models involve many users accessing unguarded models via jailbreak rather than theft, so few theft-capable employees don't materially affect risk.

excerpt: For AI R&D-4, the threat models generally do not depend on model weight theft and instead entail AI systems engaging in autonomous internal sabotage.
paraphrase: AI R&D-4 threat models mainly involve autonomous internal sabotage rather than weight theft.

excerpt: This update is a comprehensive rewrite of our RSP. For a summary of changes and the thinking behind them, see here.
paraphrase: The February 2026 update is a comprehensive rewrite, with a summary available elsewhere.

excerpt: This revision addresses the following points: (1) how we operationalize the Automated R&D capability threshold; (2) how we use internal feedback on Risk Reports; and (3) that we may consider pausing development or deployment even where the commitments described in Appendix A are not triggered.
paraphrase: The April 2026 revision addresses operationalizing the Automated R&D threshold, use of internal feedback on Risk Reports, and possible pausing outside Appendix A triggers.

excerpt: These changes are mostly clarificatory in nature; we don't see them as significant changes to substance.
paraphrase: The changes are largely clarificatory rather than substantive.

excerpt: Change (1) reflects further discussion of our operationalization of the capability threshold, and involves some substantive changes to make it better reflect our underlying intent.
paraphrase: Change (1) involves substantive changes to better reflect the intended operationalization of the threshold.

excerpt: This update also includes minor edits for style or clarity.
paraphrase: The update also includes minor stylistic and clarity edits.

excerpt: This update authorizes the LTBT to request external review of Risk Reports, gives the LTBT the power to approve our selection of external reviewers, and formalizes a requirement that we provide the LTBT with regular briefings.
paraphrase: The April 29, 2026 update lets the LTBT request external review, approve reviewer selection, and formalizes regular LTBT briefings.

excerpt: This update (1) revises our threshold for novel chemical/biological weapons production to better track the threat model of concern; (2) refines our approach to off-cycle updates regarding the risks of individual models; and (3) makes minor terminology changes.
paraphrase: The May 26, 2026 update revises the CBRN threshold, refines off-cycle update approach, and makes minor terminology changes.

excerpt: This update makes five changes:
paraphrase: The July 8, 2026 update makes five changes.

excerpt: It revises the Automated R&D capability threshold in light of further issues that have come up in discussion - particularly the question of whether we'd consider the threshold to be crossed if the overall rate of AI progress were constant or slowing, but we estimated that it was dramatically faster than it would be in the absence of advanced AI tools.
paraphrase: Change 1 revises the Automated R&D threshold, addressing whether it's crossed if progress is constant/slowing but estimated to be dramatically faster than without AI tools.

context_stem: This update makes five changes: (1) Automated R&D threshold revision.
excerpt: We would not: in this case there could be a strong argument for expecting the trend to continue rather than accelerate (if deceleration from non-AI factors continued to offset acceleration from AI-driven factors).
paraphrase: The threshold would not be considered crossed in that case, since deceleration from non-AI factors could offset AI-driven acceleration.

context_stem: This update makes five changes: (1) Automated R&D threshold revision.
excerpt: This threshold is intended to capture the onset of dramatic recursive self-improvement, and has proven difficult to operationalize.
paraphrase: The threshold aims to capture the onset of dramatic recursive self-improvement and has been hard to operationalize.

excerpt: It now requires that fully unredacted Risk Reports be shared with at least 200 Anthropic employees, rather than with all regular-clearance Anthropic staff.
paraphrase: Change 2 now requires fully unredacted Risk Reports be shared with at least 200 employees instead of all regular-clearance staff.

context_stem: This update makes five changes: (2) unredacted Risk Report sharing change.
excerpt: We will continue to share minimally-redacted Risk Reports with this latter group, but there may be some information which is both material to our risk assessment and highly sensitive to the point of meriting greater internal compartmentalization, especially in light of the company's ongoing growth.
paraphrase: Minimally-redacted Risk Reports will still go to regular-clearance staff, but some material and highly sensitive information may now warrant greater compartmentalization given company growth.

excerpt: It adjusts the scope of Risk Reports to cover Anthropic's models and activities as of a given coverage date up to 30 days prior to that report's publication.
paraphrase: Change 3 adjusts Risk Report scope to cover a coverage date up to 30 days before publication.

context_stem: This update makes five changes: (3) coverage date adjustment.
excerpt: We aim to hold our Risk Reports to a higher standard of thoroughness and coverage than our system cards while operating on a longer cadence and staying applicable over several months, and expect this change to make it easier to meet this standard without having to incorporate very recent updates to Anthropic's activities on short notice.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims for Risk Reports to be more thorough than system cards while covering longer periods, and expects this change to ease meeting that standard without last-minute updates.

excerpt: It requires us to publicly disclose, at a high level, when we make redactions in the public version of a Risk Report. Our previous Risk Report already meets this standard.
paraphrase: Change 4 requires high-level public disclosure of redactions in Risk Reports; the previous report already meets this standard.

excerpt: It clarifies that external review of our Risk Reports can involve multiple external reviewers reviewing different unredacted sections of the Risk Report, so long as all parts of the unredacted report are evaluated by at least one external reviewer.
paraphrase: Change 5 clarifies that multiple external reviewers may each review different unredacted sections, provided every part is reviewed by at least one reviewer.

excerpt: It also contains minor typo and formatting corrections.
paraphrase: The update also includes minor typo and formatting corrections.
